title: Read-Only Adoption Planner
summary: Core provides a deterministic read-only adoption planner that reports lifecycle gaps and recommended commands from cold-start discovery to explicit permanent adoption, without generating consumer policy or mutating the consumer repository.

command.syntax: shin-context [--profile CANDIDATE_PROFILE] --profile-dir PROFILE_DIR --root PROJECT adoption-plan [--marker FILE] [--agent-entry RELATIVE_FILE]
command.candidateProfile: Optional --profile identifies a human-authored permanent profile candidate. The planner validates it but never creates or rewrites it.
command.markerSelection: An explicit --marker wins and is normalized to a canonical repository-relative path when its absolute or dot-segment spelling remains below --root. Otherwise Core selects the first existing conventional marker and falls back to the canonical proposal assembled from canonicalMarkerDirectory and canonicalMarkerFile.
command.agentSelection: An explicit --agent-entry wins; otherwise AGENTS.md is the canonical proposal.
command.externalOutputTemplate: Every generated-index command uses <EXTERNAL_OUTPUT_BASE>/<INDEX_KEY>. Bootstrap may choose a temporary key; permanent adoption must substitute the exact validated marker.index.key.
command.indexAccess: The command does not read, build, or mutate a generated index and rejects --out-dir, --from-index, and --source-scan.
command.exitPolicy: A successfully generated plan returns exit 0 even when lifecycle gaps remain. Unsafe paths, malformed options, or invalid profile identifiers return shin.error.v1 with a non-zero exit.

states.not-indexable: Discovery found no supported source or machine-document evidence. Add indexable evidence before bootstrap.
states.bootstrap-ready: A strict generic bootstrap profile is available, but no permanent profile candidate or adoption marker was selected.
states.promotion-incomplete: A candidate permanent profile was supplied but one or more reviewed promotion requirements remain unresolved.
states.marker-authoring-ready: The permanent profile, eval corpus, agent entry, and path registration pass strict validation except for the intentionally absent marker file.
states.adoption-check-ready: A regular non-symlink adoption marker exists and takes precedence; adoption-check --strict remains the authority that validates its content and coherence.
states.blocked: The repository is indexable but the selected bootstrap route cannot pass strict bootstrap validation.

output.commandEncoding: Every recommended command is emitted as an argv array with writes_consumer=false so callers do not need shell parsing.
output.outputClosure: The external_output object identifies the directory template and key source. An adopter must use one external base plus the marker-owned key for every permanent command and project helper.
output.gapEncoding: Every unresolved requirement has a stable code, lifecycle stage, path or identifier, and concise summary.

requiredCandidateProperties: at least one reviewed evalCases entry
at least one representative packEvalCases entry
selected marker is registered in agentStartPaths
selected agent entry is registered in agentStartPaths
strict profile validation has no unresolved error or warning after marker creation
humanReviewRequired: one canonical external output based on marker.index.key
one project-owned adoption gate covering marker, profile, snapshot health, eval, and Pack-eval

integrationClosure.sameSnapshotPolicy: Build and every index-reading gate use <EXTERNAL_OUTPUT_BASE>/<INDEX_KEY>; after marker validation INDEX_KEY is exactly marker.index.key.
integrationClosure.legacyHelperPolicy: Existing profile-id or bootstrap helper targets must be updated or retired during cutover. A passing ad hoc command does not prove that the documented project route is coherent.
integrationClosure.plannerBoundary: The planner reports this requirement but remains read-only and does not inspect or rewrite consumer Make, shell, CI, or IDE helpers.

precedence.existingMarker: A safe existing marker produces adoption-check-ready regardless of bootstrap or candidate completeness because the marker owns the adopted route.
precedence.validator: adoption-check --strict is the only Core command that validates shin.project-adoption.v1 content, engine compatibility, permanent profile evidence, and agent-entry coherence.

security: Marker output and agent-entry input remain canonical repository-relative paths below --root; a safe explicit marker input may be normalized from another below-root spelling.
Symlink traversal and non-regular selected files are rejected.
Profile identifiers use the portable lowercase identifier policy before registry path construction.
The planner grants no source, network, process, index, or consumer-write authority.
nonGoals: No automatic profile generation or product-semantic inference.
No automatic marker or agent-entry generation.
No automatic consumer helper or CI target generation.
No replacement for discovery, profile-check, build, check, doctor, eval, pack-eval, or adoption-check.
No consumer-specific paths, identifiers, or policy in C++ Core.
